autonomy.rationale: Alejandro operates as PM with agents as his full engineering team. Agents have broad autonomy to implement across the entire codebase, constrained by explicit forbidden paths and quality gates.

forbidden_paths.reason: Real environment files contain secrets. Never read, modify, or reference.
Local environment secrets. Never read, modify, or reference.
Production secrets. Never read, modify, or reference.
Development secrets. Never read, modify, or reference.
All env files except .env.example and .env.template are forbidden. These contain real secrets.

sensitive_data_rules: Never read real .env files — only .env.example or .env.template
Never log, echo, print, or transmit environment variable values
Never hardcode secrets, API keys, tokens, or credentials in source code
Never send secret values to any external API or service
Use environment variable references (process.env.KEY_NAME) without reading actual values
security_conventions: Always parameterize database queries — no raw string concatenation or interpolation in SQL
Validate and sanitize all user input at API boundaries
No eval(), Function(), or dynamic code execution
Use CORS and helmet-style protections on Fastify
Auth checks on every protected route — never assume a request is authenticated
Never expose stack traces or internal error details to clients in production
No exposing internal service topology or infrastructure details in API responses

file_creation_rules.description: Never create markdown files unless Alejandro explicitly asks for one. Documentation belongs in GitHub issue and PR comments.

before_merge: All new code must include unit tests for services and components
All user-facing behavior must include E2E (Playwright) tests
Tests must be thorough — specific assertions, edge cases, not just happy-path
Code must pass ESLint with typescript-eslint recommended rules
Code must pass Prettier formatting (single quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 100 char print width)
Code must pass TypeScript type checking with no errors

escalation_protocols.trigger: Change requires environment variables, secrets, or API keys to be set
escalation_protocols.action: Write a step-by-step tutorial in the PR comment explaining exactly what Alejandro needs to do, where, and in what order. Treat him as a smart PM, not a senior engineer. Include platform-specific instructions (e.g., Railway dashboard, Vercel settings, GitHub Secrets).

escalation_protocols.trigger: Change requires infrastructure configuration, DNS, or third-party dashboard actions
escalation_protocols.action: Document the exact manual steps needed as a PR comment with clear instructions so Alejandro can complete them before merging.

escalation_protocols.trigger: Agent notices an unrelated improvement opportunity
escalation_protocols.action: Do not fix it. Comment on the issue describing the improvement so Alejandro can decide whether to create a separate issue.

escalation_protocols.trigger: Something in scope was skipped or could not be completed
escalation_protocols.action: Document what was skipped and why in a PR comment so Alejandro can convert it to a new issue.

github_integration.description: When @claude is invoked on an issue or PR, the default behavior is to respond as a comment. Feature docs, implementation docs, analysis, and answers are all written as comments.
github_integration.code_mode_description: Only when Alejandro explicitly says '@claude implement' should the agent create branches, write code, or open PRs. All other invocations are comment-only.

scope_discipline.description: Stay within the assigned issue scope. Do not fix unrelated issues. Do not pull work from future sprint items. Respect the sprint plan sequencing — the order is intentional.
scope_discipline.on_improvement_spotted: Comment on the issue describing the opportunity
scope_discipline.on_skipped_work: Comment on the PR describing what was not done and why

coding_conventions.description: Prettier is the formatting authority. Single quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 100 character print width. No deviations.
ESLint with typescript-eslint recommended rules. All code must pass lint with zero warnings treated seriously.
Follow existing codebase patterns and conventions. When in doubt, match what's already there.
Use pnpm exclusively. Never use npm or yarn commands.
Use Turborepo for builds and task orchestration. Respect turbo.json pipeline configuration.
Use Drizzle ORM for all database operations. Schema changes go through db:generate and db:migrate scripts.
Use Clerk for authentication. Dev bypass exists for local development. Auth checks required on all protected API routes.
AI features must be built behind provider-agnostic interfaces. No hardcoding to Anthropic, OpenAI, or any single provider. Support BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) pattern.
